tasks.short: Decide how we grade jobs and set pay when a title or CAO rule changes.

today.trigger: An HR business partner asks for a new title or a promotion rule, or a new CAO text lands on SharePoint.
steps: Find the last method note in mail or SharePoint and the matching scales in AFAS Profit.
Compare the job with the same work at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Draft the rule in Word or PowerPoint and walk it through with the HR Director.
If the grading or pay system changes, write the works-council consent note.
Tell the three HR business partners and ask payroll to store the agreed job scheme.
drudgery: Searching mail for the last agreed version of a rule.
Copying the same scale table into a fresh slide for each site.
Rewriting one decision so payroll, the HR business partners and the works council all read the same words.
today.time_sinks: Most of these 54 hours a year goes to finding the previous decision and rewriting it, not to the choice itself.

lenses.faster: Searching for the last rule and writing the first options shrink to a short check. The choice, the meeting with the HR Director and the works-council paper stay, about two thirds of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when an HR business partner files a title that is not in the scheme, or when a new CAO text is saved on SharePoint. Draft options appear on their own. The specialist stops the chain before a manager is promised a scale or the works council is written to.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the three HR business partners: a written ruling on a proposed title within a week, including a night-shift job at Venlo that today waits until the specialist is free. Demand grows if a ruling is cheap, because site managers will ask for more titles, including ones that are only a new name.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting old mail for the last version of a rule. The specialist wants more of the argument about whether two warehouse jobs are actually the same job.
lenses.options: Three drafted methods — keep the current scale, split the job, or map it to a CAO function — change which people later share a pay band.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from rewriting method slides to deciding the job architecture with the HR Director, including the right to stop a title that a site would otherwise invent. The work becomes more expert.
reach: The HR business partner's first reply to a manager who wants a new job title, once the specialist learns how that partner weighs shift coverage at the site. The offer conversation stays with the HR business partner.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can tell a real difference in the work (cold store, reach truck, a team lead's span of control) from a title made up to pay one person more. A draft that only sees the description will miss that, and a bad split becomes an unexplained pay difference later.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist and the HR Director own the method, and the works council consents when the grading or pay system changes. A model can draft options. What happens after the draft depends on that conversation, so a copilot is the simplest pattern that fits.

in_practice.trigger: An HR business partner files a title that is not in the AFAS job scheme, or a new CAO text is saved on SharePoint.
steps: The nightly extract lists incumbents and open titles in that job family, by site and scale.
A model drafts two or three options (keep the scale, split the job, map it to a CAO function) with the four factors filled from the description.
The specialist edits the option that fits the CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer or the company's warehouse CAO, and drops any option that would create an unexplained pay difference.
The HR Director agrees. Where the system or the criteria change, the specialist sends the works council the consent paper under WOR article 27(1)(c).
The agreed rule is filed on SharePoint, and payroll updates the AFAS job-scheme fields on the specialist's instruction.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist chooses the method. The HR Director agrees. The works council consents where WOR article 27(1)(c) applies. The specialist sets the scale.
data_needed: Current AFAS job scheme and scales
CAO function list and the warehouse CAO
Incumbents by site, scale and hours
Open vacancies in Recruitee for that job family
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint method file, with the draft options kept next to the decision, and the AFAS job-scheme change log.

evidence.claim: A pay or grading system needs works-council consent under WOR article 27(1)(c), unless a CAO already settles it.
Randstad's reading of the pay-transparency bill: evaluation on skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions, and works-council consent to the system, the criteria and the grouping.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as fields, in preparation for pay transparency. It is not a model.
The CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading the sector's jobs, and there is no outcome yet.
A pay decision made solely by a model is barred. A wrong grade becomes an unexplained pay difference.

risks: A draft that ignores the transport CAO or the warehouse CAO can reach the works council, or be used before consent.
If a draft recommends someone's pay or grade, it can fall under AI Act Annex III 4(b) from 2 December 2027, which brings oversight, a six-month log and telling the works council first.
A decision that is never written back into AFAS leaves Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo on different titles.
Sector regrading is still open, so an internal method may have to be redone when the CAO parties finish.
research_questions: How many title or scale requests did the three HR business partners raise in the last twelve months, and how many waited more than a month?
Which grading and pay rules are already fixed by the two CAOs, so the specialist may not redesign them?
For a change of this size, does the works council expect a consent request under WOR article 27(1)(c), or only for a wholly new system?
Can the AFAS job scheme store the four factors, or only a category code?

tasks.short: Run the equal-pay check and the link between appraisal and pay.

today.trigger: The yearly equal-pay look, a complaint about pay, or an appraisal round in which a score may move pay.
steps: Pull pay, job, hours, site and gender from AFAS into Excel.
Ask the HR business partners how appraisal scores were given, especially on the warehouse floor.
Compare people in the same job and separate CAO allowances from other differences.
Write a note for the HR Director and, where needed, sit with the manager or the works council.
File the outcome in a restricted SharePoint folder.
drudgery: Rebuilding the comparison workbook each year.
Chasing missing hours, part-time percentages and appraisal scores across three sites.
Stripping names by hand before the works council can see a table.
today.time_sinks: The hours go to cleaning the extract, and to meetings that restart because the numbers moved overnight.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the workbook drops out. Most of the task stays: the review meeting, complaints, and writing a reason for each gap the table cannot explain.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the appraisal round is closed in AFAS, or when the HR Director opens the yearly equal-pay review. The comparison report runs on its own. It stops before any pay is changed and before any name is shown to the works council.
lenses.ambitious: A decision taken at each appraisal round, rather than once a year: whether this CAO scale allows a score to move pay at all. Demand for exceptions grows if the check is cheap, and many of those requests should be refused because the scale is fixed.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the workbook and removing names by hand. The specialist wants the conversation with a manager whose scores quietly follow who they like.
lenses.options: The same population with shift allowance, overtime and age steps included or left out changes whether the works council is looking at a CAO effect or an unexplained gap, and that changes whether anyone's pay is corrected.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes a review of written reasons. The specialist gains the right to mark a difference as CAO-explained or unexplained before the HR Director considers a correction. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's written commentary on the pay page of the HR dashboard, once the specialist learns the nightly extract and who may see a row. The analyst keeps the dataset running.

tasks.human_edge: A fair reading needs the CAO reason and the warehouse context: night allowance, cold store, a certificate, a team lead's span. The specialist also has to hear a complaint from a person. The table cannot do either.
tasks.pattern_why: The equal-pay program and any link from appraisal to pay are run with the HR Director, the HR business partners and the works council. A report can draft the comparison. What to do about a gap or a complaint stays with the specialist, so a copilot is enough.

in_practice.trigger: The HR Director opens the yearly equal-pay review, a pay complaint is logged, or the appraisal round is closed in AFAS.
steps: A fixed report compares pay for people in the same AFAS job category, split by site, hours and contract, and lists gaps.
The specialist marks each gap as required by the CAO (age, shift, forklift or VCA where the scale says so) or as unexplained, and writes the reason.
Appraisal-linked pay is considered only where the CAO leaves room inside the scale. Warehouse jobs on a fixed scale are marked 'no room'.
The HR Director decides any correction. A complaint is handled in person with the HR business partner.
The works council receives the program result in the form the consent file requires, with individuals removed.
in_practice.human_gate: A person decides any correction to someone's pay, and hears every complaint. The specialist approves the text that goes to the works council.
data_needed: Pay elements, contractual hours, job category, site and gender
Age and allowance codes where the CAO uses them
Appraisal score only where the CAO allows it to affect pay
Contract type: permanent or fixed-term
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint equity file, separate from the open handbook library.

evidence.claim: Randstad's reading of the bill: a gap of 5 percent or more that stays unexplained after six months triggers a joint evaluation with the works council. Agency workers count, and agencies supply their pay data.
Works-council consent applies to a pay or grading system under WOR article 27(1)(c), with a CAO exception.
A pay decision made solely by a model is barred.
Grade or pay recommendations can fall under AI Act Annex III 4(b), high-risk from 2 December 2027.

risks: A gap that ignores CAO allowances looks like unequal treatment and can start a joint evaluation on a false basis.
Names or small-cell pay in Power BI, or in a works-council pack, breach data minimisation under the AVG.
Weak appraisal scores make a pay link look fair when the scores follow favour.
Agency workers are missing from AFAS, so the picture understates the workforce the later statutory report must cover.
research_questions: Where does each CAO leave room to move an individual inside the scale, and where is the amount fixed?
Are gender, contractual hours and allowance codes complete in AFAS at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo?
What has the works council already agreed to receive on equal pay, and is that written in a consent file?
How many pay complaints in the last two years turned on appraisal, and how many on scale placement?

tasks.short: Keep the pay handbook and the matching employee records current.

today.trigger: A CAO renewal, a pension letter, a benefits change, or HR administration asking for a handbook update.
steps: Read the new CAO article or fund letter against the current SharePoint chapter.
Retype the changed sections in Word, including allowances and pay during illness.
Check a sample of AFAS records against the chapter.
Send the draft to the HR Director and, where it sets a rule, to the works council.
HR administration publishes the PDF on SharePoint.
drudgery: Pasting CAO articles into Word and cleaning the formatting.
Checking the same allowance on a stack of contracts.
Keeping the Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo copies from drifting apart.
today.time_sinks: The slow part is making the handbook, the signed CAO and the AFAS wage components say the same thing, line by line.

lenses.faster: Retyping and the first mismatch list disappear. Reading the source against the draft, and deciding which mismatches are real exceptions, stays at a little under half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a CAO text, a pension letter or a policy is filed on SharePoint, or when a monthly check finds a wage component the handbook does not mention. The draft section and the mismatch list run unattended. Publishing, and any change in AFAS, waits for the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift team leads at the three sites get a two-page allowance sheet in plain Dutch, a group that today has only the long SharePoint handbook written for the office. Demand grows if the sheet stays two pages: supervisors will hand it out, and they will not hand out a forty-page document.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting CAO articles into Word. The specialist wants the judgment about which mismatches are real agreements and which are payroll errors.
lenses.options: A close legal draft and a plain-Dutch draft change what a team lead will apply on a Sunday night, so the version chosen changes the practice.
lenses.altitude: The specialist decides what employees are told about pay, and which records payroll must correct, and spends the week on those exceptions. The work is more expert, and it is shared with payroll.
reach: The HR administrator's update of the employment-conditions pages on SharePoint after a CAO change, once the specialist learns which pages the works council has already consented to and how the administrator publishes.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist has to catch a sentence that promises more than the CAO, the sick-pay table or the pension fund allows. Pay during illness also has to follow the Wet verbetering poortwachter calendar. A fluent paragraph can still misstate an allowance, and people will rely on it.
tasks.pattern_why: A handbook paragraph is messy source text turned into a checkable page on a fixed path: new CAO or fund letter in, draft section out, specialist approves, HR administration publishes. The record check is a query beside that step. An agent is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: A CAO text, pension letter or policy is saved on SharePoint, or the monthly wage-component check finds a code the handbook does not name.
steps: A model drafts the changed section from that source, in plain Dutch, and lists the AFAS wage components it touches.
A query lists employees whose component, scale or hours do not match the draft rule.
The specialist corrects the draft, including sick pay and the Wet verbetering poortwachter timing, and marks each mismatch as an error or an agreed exception.
The HR Director approves the chapter. Where the text sets a pay rule, the works council receives it where consent applies.
HR administration publishes the approved file. Payroll corrects only the records the specialist marked.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every chapter before it is published. Payroll changes AFAS only on the specialist's marked list.
data_needed: Signed CAO text and the current handbook chapter
AFAS wage-component catalogue, scale and site
Pension-fund letter, kept separate from the CAO text
The works council's last consent on handbook rules
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history of the handbook, plus the specialist's exception list.

evidence.claim: Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new scheme on 1 January 2027.
Whether Noordhaven's drivers are in Pensioenfonds Vervoer, and whether warehouse staff are in another fund, is not established.
A plain-language rewrite of a CAO can misstate an allowance unless a person checks it against the signed text.
Works-council consent can apply when handbook text sets a pay rule, under WOR article 27(1)(c).

risks: A plain-Dutch paragraph that contradicts the CAO will be what team leads apply.
A small team can be identified by an example salary in the handbook, which the AVG does not allow.
The pension sentence will date quickly around the January 2027 scheme, and it is wrong if drivers or warehouse staff are in a different fund.
The specialist and payroll must not be the same person changing both the rule and the record.
research_questions: Which handbook chapters has the works council consented to, and which are information only?
How many CAO or pension changes last year forced a rewrite, and how many days did each take?
Are AFAS wage-component codes stable enough to match handbook lines without a manual crosswalk?
Are drivers in Pensioenfonds Vervoer, and which fund covers the warehouse CAO population?

tasks.short: Build the organisation, grade and career-step reports managers ask for.

today.trigger: The HR Director, the works council or a site manager asks for a picture of jobs, grades or career steps, usually a few times a year.
steps: Export jobs, managers, scales and sites from AFAS to Excel.
Draw the organisation chart and the grade table in PowerPoint or Excel.
Add career steps from memory and from what recruiters have been telling candidates.
Reconcile headcount to payroll and remove people the audience should not see.
Send a PDF and file it on SharePoint.
drudgery: Redrawing boxes because a manager link is broken.
Rebuilding the same grade table for the HR Director, a site and the works council.
Fixing titles that were typed differently at each site.
today.time_sinks: The time goes to drawing and reconciling, not to deciding what the chart means.

lenses.faster: Drawing the chart and rebuilding the grade table drop out once the nightly extract feeds a saved report. The exception list and a short release check stay, about a third of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: It starts on the nightly AFAS refresh, or when the HR Director asks for the current picture. The charts refresh without the specialist. A chart is not sent outside HR until the specialist has cleared broken manager links, missing scales and people who should not be on it.
lenses.ambitious: Venlo warehouse managers get their own grade and career-step chart, a site that today works from a Rotterdam file. Demand grows if the chart is a refresh rather than a drawing: Tilburg, and then the night shift, will ask for the same cut.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss dragging boxes in a slide. The specialist wants the argument about which two jobs are actually one career step apart.
lenses.options: A chart grouped by CAO function and a chart grouped by the site's own titles show different career steps, and that choice changes which promotion path the company will stand behind.
lenses.altitude: This time goes to jobs that do not fit the chart. The specialist gains the right to withhold a report that still has broken manager or scale data. Reading the chart is more expert work than drawing it.
reach: The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's monthly grade-distribution page, once the specialist learns the extract's field names and the rule for who may see pay. The analyst keeps the refresh running.

tasks.human_edge: A broken line is often a real fact: one team lead shared across two sites, or an agency worker who must not appear as an employee. The specialist has to recognise that before anyone trusts the chart.
tasks.pattern_why: An organisation chart, a grade distribution and a career-step table are queries over AFAS once the job architecture is stored. No model call is required. The specialist clears exceptions and decides who may see the report.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract refreshes, or the HR Director asks for the current picture.
steps: People Analytics refreshes grade, span and site charts from the extract, using rules the specialist has written down.
Rows with no manager, no scale or a scale outside the scheme land on an exception list.
The specialist has HR administration or payroll correct the source, or records a named exception.
Career steps are taken only from the approved job architecture, not from titles typed in Recruitee.
The specialist releases the report to the HR Director. Pay and names stay off any chart that goes wider.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist releases every report that leaves HR and decides each exception.
data_needed: Position, manager, job category, scale, site and FTE
Contract type, so agency workers are not drawn as employees
The approved career steps from the job architecture
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI refresh log and the exception list on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as fields, in preparation for pay transparency.
A chart built from ungoverned local titles will not match the job scheme, and people will treat it as one.
Randstad's reading of the bill requires job categories that can support a later pay report, including agency workers.

risks: Career steps copied from recruiter promises will not match the CAO or the scheme.
A Power BI workspace that shows pay to a wide audience breaches the AVG.
Agency headcount is omitted or drawn as employment, so the three sites look the wrong size.
A pretty chart gets treated as a new grading system without works-council consent.
research_questions: Do manager, job category and scale arrive complete in the nightly extract for all three sites?
Who can open the HR Power BI workspace today, and does it already show pay?
How are the 150 to 300 agency workers stored, if they are stored at all?
Which career steps do recruiters already promise that are not in the approved scheme?

tasks.short: Find out what a job really requires and whether it has changed.

today.trigger: A manager says a job has changed, a new role is proposed, or a grading round is about to start.
steps: Read the current description, the CAO function profile and the Recruitee vacancy text.
Interview the manager and, where the floor disagrees, an incumbent.
Look for the same work at the other two sites.
Note certificates, shift, cold store and physical load.
Write a requirements note and file it with the job.
drudgery: Rereading long descriptions that repeat each other.
Hunting equivalent jobs across three sites in Excel.
Rewriting interview notes into the same headings every time.
today.time_sinks: Travel and waiting for floor interviews take the calendar time. Rewriting notes takes most of the desk time.

lenses.faster: The first comparison against the CAO profile and the sister jobs appears as a draft. Floor interviews and the manager conversation stay, and they are still more than half of this task.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a recruiter or HR business partner files a new or changed job against an AFAS job code. The comparison draft is ready before the specialist opens the file. Nothing is graded, and no candidate is promised a scale, until the specialist decides the core job has actually changed.
lenses.ambitious: The decision 'have the core accountabilities changed enough to regrade?' is taken when a team rewrites a job around a new warehouse system or new software, not only in a yearly batch. Demand for regrades grows if the check is cheap, and most of those requests should end as 'do not regrade'.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss lining up three descriptions under homemade headings. The specialist wants the floor interview, where the real working conditions show up.
lenses.options: One draft that says the job changed, and one that says only the tools changed, lead to opposite decisions on whether a regrade even opens.
lenses.altitude: The week on this task becomes short interviews and a yes-or-no on opening a regrade, with the comparison already on the page. The specialist gains the right to refuse a regrade when the core job is the same. The work is more expert.
reach: The recruiter's first draft of the requirements on a Recruitee vacancy, for jobs already in the scheme, once the specialist learns which fields the career site publishes. The recruiter keeps the candidate process.

tasks.human_edge: Nights, cold, physical load and lone work in an aisle are easy to understate in a text written to attract candidates. The specialist has to test that text on the floor. A UK pilot that scored descriptions alone was a bit over seventy percent in line with experts, and it did not measure time.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is messy — a vacancy, a CAO profile, a manager's claim — and the output is a checkable comparison under four fixed factors. One drafting step on that path is enough. The interview and the decision to open a regrade stay with the specialist.

in_practice.trigger: A new or changed job is filed in Recruitee against an AFAS job code.
steps: The specialist pulls the current AFAS job, the CAO profile and the vacancy text.
A model drafts a comparison under skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions, and lists the facts that are missing. The draft does not assign a scale.
The specialist interviews the manager or an incumbent where the draft shows a gap, especially on shift and physical load.
The specialist decides whether core accountabilities changed. If they did not, the job is not regraded.
The note, the draft and the decision are filed together on the job.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides whether the core job changed enough to open a grading. The draft does not set a scale.
data_needed: Current job description and CAO function text
Recruitee vacancy text
Required certificates, site and shift
Sister jobs at the other sites
in_practice.logs_to: The job file on SharePoint, with the model draft kept beside the specialist's decision.

evidence.claim: A UK university pilot scored 50 job descriptions with ChatGPT, one model per HERA factor. Agreement with experts exceeded 70 percent. Time was not measured. The pilot was self-reported.
If core accountabilities have not materially changed, do not regrade. AI use on its own should not trigger a series of one-off job evaluations.
Of 500 employers in an August 2026 opt-in panel, 61 percent were rewriting job descriptions for AI, 49 percent said salary structures lag, and 48 percent said benchmarks miss AI skills.
Randstad's reading of the bill sets the four factors as skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions.
A wrong grade becomes an unexplained pay difference.

risks: Treating a seventy-percent pilot on university descriptions as good enough to grade a warehouse job.
Regrading because the software changed, then being unable to explain the pay difference.
Vacancy text written to attract candidates will understate working conditions and poison the draft.
The sector CAO regrade is still open, so an internal conclusion may have to move again.
research_questions: In past regrades, how often had the core accountabilities actually changed, as opposed to the tools or the title?
Are AFAS and Recruitee descriptions complete enough to fill the four factors, or too thin to draft from?
Will managers accept a refusal to regrade when only the software has changed?
When are the CAO parties expected to finish the sector regrade, and does that make an internal exercise premature?

tasks.short: Build the questionnaires and interview scripts used to grade jobs.

today.trigger: A grading round is opening, or the current descriptions are too thin to grade.
steps: Decide whether this job family needs a questionnaire, an interview or time on the floor.
Write the questions in Word from the last grading.
Pilot them with one HR business partner and one manager.
Rewrite after the pilot and store the form on SharePoint.
Chase answers and file them with the job.
drudgery: Rewriting the same questions for each job family.
Turning free-text answers into the same factors by hand.
Chasing managers who do not return the form.
today.time_sinks: Design cycles and the wait for answers take more time than the thinking about what to measure.

lenses.faster: Writing the first questionnaire and script shrinks to an edit. Choosing the method, piloting it on a real warehouse job, and a works-council step if the criteria change, stay at about three fifths of the time.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a grading file has empty factors, or when a grading round is opened. A draft instrument is waiting. It is not sent to managers until the specialist has cut it and, where the criteria are new, the works council has consented.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift order pickers and reach-truck drivers, whose descriptions were copied from the day shift, are interviewed on their own working conditions. Demand grows if the script fits in a handover: supervisors will allow that, where they will not allow a long survey.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rewriting the same questions for the tenth job family. The specialist wants the pilot, where a question that looked clever fails on the floor.
lenses.options: A short handover script and a long factor form collect different facts about effort and working conditions, and those facts can move a later grade.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns what gets measured and can refuse a grading that rests on a day-shift copy of a night job. Designing a fair instrument is more expert work than typing one.
reach: The Learning and Development Specialist's build of this one short survey in Studytube or Forms, once the specialist learns how a survey is published and how completion is stored. The course catalogue stays with Learning and Development.

tasks.human_edge: A question that works for an office planner fails for a reach-truck driver at 03:00. The specialist hears that in the pilot. A complete-looking form can still ask the wrong people, or ask for pay history, which the bill as Randstad reads it would forbid.
tasks.pattern_why: An instrument is a known kind of output from approved criteria. One draft mapped to the four factors is checkable. Choosing survey, interview or floor observation, and freezing the questions, stays with the specialist.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist opens a grading round, or a job file cannot fill the four factors from the description.
steps: A model drafts a short questionnaire and an interview script from the last works-council-approved criteria, mapped to skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions.
The specialist removes any question about pay history and any question a shift supervisor will not answer straight.
One HR business partner pilots it on one office job and one warehouse job.
The specialist freezes the instrument. If the criteria themselves change, the works council consents before it is used.
Answers are stored against the job, not in personal mail.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist freezes the instrument. New criteria go to the works council before use. The instrument is not scored by a model into a grade.
data_needed: The criteria the works council last consented to
CAO function profiles and two or three example jobs
The last consent text, so the draft does not quietly change it
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint instrument folder, with the version and the pilot notes.

evidence.claim: Randstad's reading of the bill: four factors, works-council consent to the criteria, and no question about salary history.
WOR article 27(1)(c) requires works-council consent for a grading system, unless a CAO settles it.
The UK pilot graded from existing descriptions, one model per factor, and still disagreed with experts on part of the set. Thin descriptions need a better instrument.
A fluent questionnaire can still ask the wrong people the wrong things.

risks: A question about previous pay slips through and conflicts with the salary-history ban in Randstad's reading of the bill.
The instrument quietly changes the criteria without works-council consent.
Answers stored with employee names, where the job fact was all that was needed, breach the AVG.
If a model later scores the form into a grade, that use can be high-risk from 2 December 2027 and the works council should be told first.
research_questions: What did the works council last consent to as evaluation criteria, and may this round reuse it?
Will night-shift supervisors give fifteen minutes at handover on all three sites?
Are current warehouse descriptions copies of the day shift? A short sample would confirm or kill the case for a new floor script.
Does any form in use today ask for previous pay?

tasks.short: Turn pay data into figures for finance, the works council and regulators.

today.trigger: The budget cycle, a works-council question, a CAO wage talk, or a request for figures from outside the company.
steps: Pull pay and headcount from AFAS into Excel.
Add CAO rates, allowances and holiday pay, and try to match finance's totals.
Compute averages and simple gaps by job and site.
Write a note for the HR Director, the controller or the works council.
Rebuild the sheet when the next question arrives.
drudgery: Reconciling the HR extract to the general ledger.
Repeating the same cut for each site.
Footnoting every allowance so the average is not misread.
today.time_sinks: Each follow-up question triggers another rebuild. That rebuild, not the conclusion, takes the hours.

lenses.faster: The rebuild for each new cut disappears once the calculation is fixed. Writing the reason for an unexplained gap, and answering the works council, stays at about half the task.
lenses.autonomous: It starts on the nightly refresh and on a date the controller or the HR Director sets. The tables update without the specialist. A table leaves the team only after the specialist has signed the version and the flag for missing agency data.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the works council: a quarterly note of unexplained gaps by site, started before the first statutory report (on Randstad's reading, 2027 pay, due by 7 June 2028), so a large gap is discussed while there is still time. Demand grows if a refresh is cheap: the works council will ask for shift and contract-type cuts it does not ask for while each cut is a new workbook.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss forcing the HR workbook and the finance workbook to match. The specialist wants the part where a remaining gap gets a real reason, or a real correction.
lenses.options: The same pay bill with overtime in or out, and with or without the agency file, can push a group over or under the 5 percent unexplained line in Randstad's reading of the bill. That changes whether a joint evaluation would start.
lenses.altitude: The week on this task becomes the unexplained remainder and the conversation with finance and the works council. The specialist gains the right to mark a figure as complete or as missing agency data. Judging the remainder is more expert than assembling it.
reach: The FP&A analyst's first costing of a CAO wage increase into the personnel budget, once the specialist learns the planning calendar and how AFAS payroll ties to the general ledger. The FP&A analyst keeps the forecast.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can tell a CAO allowance from an unexplained difference, and can say when the file is too incomplete to show the works council. An average that looks precise will hide a missing Venlo night shift or a missing agency file.
tasks.pattern_why: The gap and the CAO cost are arithmetic on agreed fields and written rules. A model is the wrong tool for a figure that may be shown to the works council or a regulator. The specialist writes the reason for whatever the arithmetic cannot classify.

in_practice.trigger: The controller's budget calendar, a works-council request, or, once the law is in force, the statutory reporting date.
steps: A documented calculation on the nightly extract produces headcount, pay, allowances and a gap by job category, site and gender, with CAO components shown on their own.
Agency-worker rows are included only when the three staffing agencies have supplied a file in an agreed layout. Otherwise the report marks the gap in coverage.
The specialist reviews categories with a large unexplained difference and writes the reason or the open question.
Finance uses the same cost totals for a CAO scenario, so HR and the controller share one definition of pay.
The specialist sends the note. Individual pay stays out of anything that goes to the works council or outside the company.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist signs any figure that leaves the team. A person writes the reason for an unexplained gap. The calculation does not recommend a pay change.
data_needed: Pay elements, hours, job category, gender, site and contract
Written CAO rules for allowances, age steps and holiday pay
Agency pay files when the agencies supply them
The finance definition of personnel cost in the general ledger
in_practice.logs_to: The report archive on SharePoint, with the extract date and the calculation version.

evidence.claim: Randstad's reading of the bill: yearly report, first on 2027 pay, by 7 June 2028; debates in December 2026 and January 2027; start by royal decree; agency workers included; requests answered in two months; a 5 percent unexplained gap after six months triggers a joint evaluation with the works council; fines up to €11,000.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as fields for pay-transparency preparation.
A pay decision made solely by a model is barred. A statistical note is not itself a pay decision; a recommendation to change someone's pay is different.
Grade or pay recommendations can be high-risk under AI Act Annex III 4(b) from 2 December 2027.

risks: A 5 percent figure from incomplete data can start a joint evaluation, and a fine of up to €11,000, on a false basis.
Gender or pay in a wide Power BI workspace breaches the AVG.
If HR and finance keep two definitions of pay, the report will not be trusted.
Agency files will arrive late or on different job codes, and forcing them into Noordhaven's categories will invent gaps.
research_questions: Can finance and HR agree one definition of pay — base, allowances, overtime, holiday pay — that would also serve the transparency report?
What share of employees today has a complete job category and gender in AFAS at each site?
Will the three agencies sign a file layout, a date and an AVG processing arrangement for pay data?
If the bill's timetable slips, does the works council still want a quarterly gap note under today's equal-treatment practice?

tasks.short: Teach managers the pay, allowance and pension rules they must apply.

today.trigger: A CAO or pension change, a manager who has been mis-explaining pay, or Learning and Development's yearly course list.
steps: Agree the audience with Learning and Development.
Rebuild last year's PowerPoint from the handbook.
Deliver a daytime session, usually at Rotterdam.
Answer the same questions by mail for weeks afterwards.
File the deck on SharePoint and, sometimes, ask for a Studytube page.
drudgery: Rebuilding last year's slides after a small CAO change.
Repeating the same allowance explanation to people who missed the session.
Collecting attendance so the session counts as done.
today.time_sinks: Deck production, plus a session the warehouse does not attend, followed by one-to-one explanations to team leads.

lenses.faster: Building the first deck from the approved handbook chapter shrinks to an edit. Travel, the live session and the follow-up questions stay, about three quarters of this task.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when an approved handbook chapter changes, or when Learning and Development opens the course list. Draft notes appear on their own. Nothing is published in Studytube, and nothing is said to managers, until the specialist has corrected it.
lenses.ambitious: Warehouse team leads on the night shift, who do not come to the Rotterdam daytime session, get a twenty-minute handover briefing on what they may tell a new hire about scale and allowances. Demand grows if it stays inside the handover: leads at Tilburg and Venlo will ask for it, and they will keep calling HR if it does not exist.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding last year's slides. The specialist wants the live questions, where a team lead says what they have been promising on the floor.
lenses.options: A version that stresses fixed CAO scales and a version that stresses the small room for discretion lead managers to different promises, and those promises show up in offers.
lenses.altitude: Teaching time moves to the people who actually quote pay, on shift. The specialist gains the right to decide what Learning and Development may publish about pay. The job stays expert, because what managers repeat is still the specialist's responsibility.
reach: The Learning and Development Specialist's upkeep of one Studytube module on pay rules for managers, once the specialist learns how Studytube records completion. Forklift, VCA and food-safety courses stay with Learning and Development.

tasks.human_edge: In the room, a team lead tests the edges: a night allowance, a promotion that is really a favour, a pension question that depends on one driver's service. The specialist answers from the CAO and that situation. A slide cannot. A chatbot that tried would have to say it is AI, and it would still not decide pay.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist stays the person who trains managers, because a wrong answer becomes a promise about pay. A model can draft notes from an approved chapter. That is assistance inside the specialist's session, not a workflow that should run out to employees on its own.

in_practice.trigger: An approved handbook chapter changes, Learning and Development opens the catalogue, or the same manager question has arrived three times.
steps: A model drafts a short session plan and speaker notes from that approved chapter only, and quotes the chapter where the wording matters.
The specialist corrects anything that goes past the CAO, the sick-pay rules or the fund letter.
Learning and Development puts the approved material in Studytube for office staff who need a completion record.
The specialist runs the live conversation for HR business partners and for warehouse team leads, including a short handover version on nights.
Questions the notes cannot answer go back into the handbook task, rather than being answered with a new promise.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every teaching text before it is published or said aloud. A person's own pay question is answered by the specialist.
data_needed: The approved handbook chapter
The CAO articles and the pension-fund letter
The list of managers and team leads who make offers or quote pay
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube completion for the recorded module, and the deck version on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: A benefits chatbot must say it is AI.
For a high-risk system, workers' representatives are informed first, and logs are kept.
Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new scheme on 1 January 2027, so pension teaching dated before that letter will be wrong for members of that fund.
Managers repeat what a session appeared to allow, including discretion the CAO does not give.

risks: A Studytube module from an unapproved draft will be treated as the pay rule.
Training that implies discretion the CAO does not give will show up in offers the recruiters make.
The night-shift briefing becomes a second, divergent policy if it is not the same approved chapter.
A benefits bot added later, without saying it is AI and without telling the works council, breaks the transparency rule and the trust of the room.
research_questions: How many pay questions last year came from warehouse team leads, and how many from office managers?
Will night-shift supervisors give twenty minutes at handover at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo?
Is there already a Studytube module on employment conditions, and who may edit it?
Which answers are already fixed by the CAO, so the session must not present them as a local choice?

role.altitude: The specialist moves from grading one job and rebuilding one workbook at a time to owning Noordhaven's job architecture and the written reason for every pay difference that remains after the CAOs are applied, at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
reach: The recruiter's salary-band text on a vacancy, once the band is already approved and the specialist learns the Recruitee fields the career site shows. The recruiter keeps the candidate relationship.
The payroll specialist's update of wage-component codes after a CAO agreement, once the specialist can read a payroll test run. Payroll still runs the month close.
The FP&A analyst's CAO wage scenario in the personnel budget, using the same definition of pay as the gap figures. The analyst keeps the forecast.
The HR business partner's scale check before an offer goes out, inside an approved band. The partner keeps the conversation with the manager.
role.ceiling_note: There is one specialist, three sites, and night shifts they do not work. Works-council consent and the CAO calendar set the pace. These eight tasks are about a fifth of the year; individual pay questions, pension cases and meetings fill the rest and compress less. The specialist must not be the only control on a pay change: payroll posts it and the HR Director approves exceptions. Agency pay stays with three staffing firms until they supply it. A model may not decide pay, and from 2 December 2027 a grading or pay recommendation can be high-risk. The pension scheme itself belongs to the fund.
skills_to_grow: Writing a grade reason under the four factors so a later gap report can reuse it.
AFAS job schemes, wage components and the nightly extract, well enough to specify a check People Analytics can build.
The pay-transparency file: what the works council has consented to, what an employee may ask, and the two-month clock in Randstad's reading of the bill.
Reading a Pensioenfonds Vervoer letter and a payroll test run, without taking over the month close.
Filing the draft and the human decision together, so a grading aid can meet a six-month log and a prior talk with the works council if it becomes high-risk on 2 December 2027.
role.ambitious_version: One job architecture covers the three sites. Recruiters publish a band that already exists. HR business partners get a yes or no on a new title without inventing a scale. The works council sees unexplained gaps, including agency workers when the agencies supply pay, in time to act before a statutory report. Night-shift team leads hear the same pay rules as the office. The specialist's week is disputed jobs, CAO changes and those conversations.
